html:
Ne Win was the general who seized power in Burma on 2 March 1962 and ruled it for 26 years. One of the Thirty Comrades trained by Japan with Aung San, he built the army into the country's master.

He nationalised business, expelled hundreds of thousands of Indians, closed Burma to the world and followed a Burmese Way to Socialism. Once among the richest countries in Southeast Asia, Burma became one of the poorest.

In 1987 he cancelled most banknotes, wiping out people's savings, which helped set off the 8888 Uprising. He resigned in 1988, but the army kept power. See Karen conflict and Panglong.
